Fix documentation references to ANSI C.

Originally IMath was written to be compatible with ANSI C89, or the equivalent
ISO/IEC 9899:1990 ("C90"). After #29, however, it is no longer accurate to use
the label "ANSI", since later versions of C are published by ISO. Update the
docs to avoid this misuse.

Tag release 1.31.

There are no functional changes in this release. Other than some documentation
cleanup, the main changes are the addition of a Travis CI configuration, and
some fixes to the Makefile.

Update instructions for reporting bugs.

Because it is no longer the Dark Ages, people can just use the issue tracker
instead of sending me e-mail like we were animals.

Fix the example code in the Dockerfile.

Copy files into the build container.

Instead of mapping over the local filesystem, copy the build context into the
container and run the build there. The local state can still pollute the build
image, but make clean should take care of that, and this way we don't wind up
with .o files from the wrong architecture.

Updates #27. A very simple test plan that simply runs "make check" for each
interesting configuration. Right now the "interesting" configurations are macOS
(because I use it) and Linux (because everyone uses it), and the latter with
both Clang and GCC.

I had to update test.sh to be explicitly Bash rather than Bourne, since on
macOS "sh" is an alias for Bash but not so in Ubuntu.

Tag release 1.30.

Improve test automation; no functional changes to the library.
Add a docker-test target to the Makefile.
Add a .gitattributes file.

Make the Linux test protocol less brittle.

Instead of running the tests as part of the build, bind mount the imath host
directory into the container. This way you do not need to rebuild the container
each time you make changes -- or at least will get a cached result.

imtest: Make test output easier to read.

Each failed line now includes the filename the test came from, or "-" if the
test case was from stdin. Errors in parsing will now also report a failing exit
status. Only one line per input file is now logged with the totals.

Updates #27.

test.sh: Exit non-zero if any unit tests fail.

Previously the script was ignoring the results from failed tests.  This forces
the script to exit with an error if that happens. It also filters out more of
the diagnostic noise from the program.

Updates #27.

imtest: Ensure the exit code is non-zero when tests fail.

When processing named input files, we were correctly setting the exit status,
but not when processing stdin. While I was in there, I added doc comments to
the various support functions, since I had to re-understand them to make sure I
was doing it right.

Add functions to set default precision and multiply threshold.

Rather than forcing the caller to play games with linking, add functions to set

imath: Drop switchable statics and stdio dependency.

Prior to this commit, defining DEBUG switched the static helper functions to
have external linkage. As far as I can tell nobody is making use of this.
Moreover, that switch exports two "print" functions that I used a lot when
debugging the initial library, but haven't done anything with in a long time.
Remove all that noise, and update the documentation.

Strictly speaking this is a breaking change, but only under DEBUG=Y, so I do
not feel it's necessary to protect it.
imtimer: Fix a lingering lvalue use of MP_USED.

Rework the handling of temporaries.

The temp-handling macros had a very brittle structure: DECLARE_TEMP injects
multiple variables into the scope, while SETUP expects a particular name to be
present for its own use, shared with CLEANUP_TEMP.

Rework these to reduce (though not eliminate) the problem:

 - DECLARE_TEMP now creates a single temp_ struct, and all the details of temp
   handling live in that struct.

 - LAST_TEMP has been removed: All temps are now initialized to zero without
   allocation.

 - SETUP has been renamed to REQUIRE, and is more general -- it works for any
   expression of type mp_result, and handles cleanup correctly.

 - The shared error state for REQUIRE and CLEANUP_TEMP is now in the managed
   struct, so the enclosing function does not need to maintain any magic
   variables.

 - Rework function bodies in terms of REQUIRE.
   Wherever it is practical to do so, replace control flow like

      if ((res = <expression>) != MP_OK) goto CLEANUP;

   with the equivalent but easier-to-read:

      REQUIRE(<expression>);

   This can only be done where there is a temp manager on the stack, but it
   turns out most of the functions that have "interesting" control flow also
   have at least one temporary.

Updates #29. Strictly speaking this isn't making use of variable-length arrays,
but it satisfies the desire underlying that request to better-isolate storage
